items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 names the class RedStoneWireBlock (capital S; jar-verified - net/minecraft/world/level/block/RedStoneWireBlock.class exists, RedstoneWireBlock does not; the class file is byte-identical to 26.1's). The prepared 26.1.1 data is faithful: block-behaviours.json carries redstone_wire's class chain as ["RedStoneWireBlock", "Block"]. But the port's class table (level/classes.rs:224, byte-identical to 26.1's) knows only "RedstoneWireBlock", and the 26.1.1 tree has no alias mechanism at all (unlike the 26.2 tree, which has RedstoneWire = "RedstoneWireBlock" | "RedStoneWireBlock" plus a unit test). Class::from_java returns None for the real name, so level/data.rs:920-928 drops it from the chain and the wire resolves to Class::Block. Every wire arm exists but never runs: hooks.rs:100 (neighborChanged -> wire_update_power), hooks.rs:211 (onPlace), hooks.rs:380 (affectNeighborsAfterRemoval), shapes.rs:698 (updateShape), redstone.rs:65,101 (signal), interact.rs:263, place.rs:1089, survive.rs:281. Wire power stays 0, wire emits no signal. The wire logic itself matches vanilla 26.1.1 method-for-method (see report Passes); the defect is the one-line table miss. The prepare-side half is unfixed too: crates/horizon-prepare/src/survival.rs:43 still reads ("RedstoneWireBlock", "RedstoneWire"). 26.1 B2-G01 and 1.21.7 G7 reproduce in 26.1.1. A full class-table census (all 1,168 exported blocks vs the 271 known classes) finds exactly three blocks resolving to plain Block despite a non-Block chain: redstone_wire (this item), dirt_path (DirtPathBlock) and amethyst_block (AmethystBlock) - the latter two are out of Batch 2 scope.
items.title: Redstone wire completely non-functional: class-name mismatch (RedStoneWireBlock vs RedstoneWireBlock)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1's PushReaction enum is NORMAL, DESTROY, BLOCK, IGNORE, PUSH_ONLY (jar-verified - the pre-26.3 names; the class is byte-identical to 26.1's). The prepared 26.1.1 gameplay-facts.json carries exactly those names: NORMAL 22,869 states, DESTROY 6,849, BLOCK 91, PUSH_ONLY 64 (no IGNORE states exist in 26.1.1). But the loader (level/data.rs:886-890) matches only the 26.3 names - "PUSH", "POPPED", "IMMOVEABLE", "IGNORE_ENTITY" - and defaults everything else to PushPull. All 29,873 states load as PushPull. Census (evidence/census_nibbles_26_1_1.py, state->block map from the 26.1.1 datagen blocks.json): 355 DESTROY blocks (torches, wire, flowers, buttons, doors, beds, shulker boxes, comparators, repeaters, levers, ...) are pushed instead of popped with no DropResources event; 13 BLOCK blocks (anvils, grindstone, lodestone, piston, sticky_piston, piston_head, moving_piston, barrier, end/nether portals, end gateway) are pushed instead of blocking the move; 16 PUSH_ONLY blocks (all glazed terracotta) become pullable by sticky pistons. The is_pushable reaction switch itself (pistons.rs:368-372) matches vanilla's switch map exactly - it simply never sees a non-PushPull value. 26.1 B2-G02 and 1.21.7 G8 reproduce in 26.1.1.
items.title: Push-reaction loader mapping matches no 26.1.1 value: every state loads as PushPull

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 PistonBaseBlock.isPushable (net.minecraft.world.level.block.piston.PistonBaseBlock, jar-verified fresh - evidence/pistonbase.txt) refuses OBSIDIAN, CRYING_OBSIDIAN, RESPAWN_ANCHOR and REINFORCED_DEEPSLATE explicitly before the reaction switch (bytecode offsets 44-85). All four are NORMAL reaction with hardness != -1 (obsidian hardness 50.0), so nothing else in the check stops them. The port (level/pistons.rs:328-372, byte-identical to 26.1's) has no such check - grep obsidian pistons.rs returns nothing - and the 26.2 tree's obsidian block (pistons.rs:344-355 there, with the comment noting 26.3 gave them IMMOVEABLE instead) is absent from the 26.1.1 tree, as are the crying_obsidian / reinforced_deepslate named entries in data.rs (the table has obsidian at :267 and respawn_anchor at :369, but neither of the other two). A piston extends and pushes obsidian instead of staying retracted. 26.1 B2-G03 and 1.21.7 G9 reproduce in 26.1.1.
items.title: is_pushable lacks vanilla's hardcoded obsidian-family refusal

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 PistonBaseBlock.isPushable (net.minecraft.world.level.block.piston.PistonBaseBlock, jar-verified fresh - evidence/pistonbase.txt) bounds-checks y > maxY (320; overworld dimension_type min_y -64 + height 384) and refuses only UP-pushes from y == maxY (bytecode offsets 0-34 and 106-125). The port uses max_y = level.max_y() - 1 (319) at level/pistons.rs:337 (byte-identical to 26.1's), so it refuses y == 320 outright and refuses UP-pushes from y == 319. A piston at y == 319 pushing up fails in the port where vanilla extends. Floor side matches vanilla exactly. 26.1 B2-G04 and 1.21.7 G10 reproduce in 26.1.1. Same defect as 26.2's B2-G01.
items.title: is_pushable Y-bound off by one at the ceiling

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 DiodeBlock.neighborChanged has NO same-block guard: the method goes straight to canSurvive (bytecode offset 0), then checkTickOnNeighbor, else dropResources + removeBlock + updateNeighborsAt in all directions (fresh javap, evidence/diode.txt, offsets 0-94; the class is byte-identical to 26.1's). The 26.1 tree carries this correctly - its redstone.rs has an explicit comment noting 26.1 has no guard and 26.2 returns early. The 26.1.1 tree instead carries the 26.2 form: level/redstone.rs:673-675 returns early when the block at the position is no longer the diode (if !self.b.is_block(self.state(pos), block) { return; }). This is the ONLY behavioural difference in redstone.rs between the 26.1 and 26.1.1 trees (full diff: the 4-line 26.1 comment deleted, the 3-line guard added). Effect: when a neighbour change is delivered to a diode position whose block has already been replaced, vanilla 26.1.1 still runs the survive/tick path on the passed state (and drops the diode's resources + notifies neighbours if it cannot survive), while the port silently does nothing. NEW vs 26.1 - the 26.1 run counted this as a pass; it is a regression in the 26.1.1 tree and the clearest in-scope instance of the stale-carry problem (see systemic_note).
items.title: DiodeBlock.neighborChanged carries the 26.2 same-block guard vanilla 26.1.1 does not have

items.evidence: Batch 0 measurement (docs/sweep/26.1.1/batch-0-oracles.json): fails on all three classpaths, 32 errors, first error '450: cannot find symbol' - identical to 26.1. Anatomy (26.1 recompile): net.minecraft.world.level.blockscan absent from 26.1.1 (5 errors: 319, 322, 411, 427, 444; 0 jar entries - findBlocksIn does not exist on Level/ServerLevel either); net.minecraft.util.Continuation absent (3 errors: 436, 439, 442); net.minecraft.world.clock.ClockInstance absent (2 errors at 450, + 4 no-override at 451-454); no-override: findBlocksIn x2, getNextEntityId (357, absent from Level/ServerLevel), Scan overrides x6, ClockInstance methods x4, getCommandSpamThresholdSeconds / getChatSpamThresholdSeconds (530, 531 - absent from 26.1.1's MinecraftServer); MinecraftServer ctor (508 - oracle calls the 11-arg super with the 26.3 NotificationManager slot; 26.1.1's ctor is 10-arg); ServerChunkCache ctor (621 - oracle calls 10-arg super; 26.1.1's ctor is 11-arg); 1 non-static-super (424) + 3 statePredicate (436, 442, 445). Gone vs 1.21.7's O1: operatorUserPermissions() and getFunctionCompilationPermissions() exist in 26.1.1's MinecraftServer, and environmentAttributes() exists on 26.1.1's Level. Blocks test_redstone_parity (via block_update_harness.py) plus 5 other drivers, and anchors 6 cascade oracles. 26.1 B2-O01 and 1.21.7 O1 reproduce in 26.1.1.

The prepared-data precondition that blocked 26.2's H01/H02 is MET for 26.1.1 (.local/horizon-client/26.1.1/ exists with block-behaviours.json + gameplay-facts.json), and the nibble/press-time checks 26.2 deferred to H01 were run here as real checks (see report Passes). items.evidence: level/tests.rs carries redstone_lever_wire_and_lamp (:1253), levers_power_wire_through_interaction (:1734), pistons_push_and_sticky_pistons_pull (:1781) and pistons_pop_fragile_blocks_and_refuse_obsidian (:2120) - the file is byte-identical to 26.1's. Unlike 26.2, where the root causes were fixed and the tests were expected to pass, for 26.1.1 three of the four are expected to FAIL: the two wire tests on B2-G01 (wire power stays 0), the piston-pop test on B2-G02 (torch pushed, no DropResources event) and B2-G03 (obsidian pushed). The push/pull test is expected to pass (dirt is NORMAL reaction either way). No cargo builds were allowed in this batch (shared 6 GB VM), so a test run is still needed to confirm behaviourally. Note the tests load the real prepared resources and silently skip (the world!() macro returns early) when .local is absent - which is why the 26.1.1 crate-tests CI run could go green while these defects stand: a clean runner has no prepared data, so the level tests never ran there. A run with HORIZON_RESOURCES pointed at the prepared 26.1.1 data (present in this worktree) is what would demonstrate the failures. 26.1 B2-H02 reproduces in 26.1.1.
items.title: The 4 level::tests need a cargo test run (3 expected to fail on B2-G01/B2-G02/B2-G03)

items.evidence: 1.21.7's G11 was that vanilla takes the item frame first and the port takes max(frame, block). In 26.1.1 vanilla CHANGED (same as 26.1 and 26.2): ComparatorBlock.getInputSignal (bytecode offset 150, Math.max, fresh javap in evidence/comparator.txt) computes Math.max(frameAnalogOrMIN, blockAnalogOrMIN) and uses it unless both are absent - vanilla 26.1.1 takes the max, exactly as the port does (level/redstone.rs:541-546). The port matches 26.1.1; no defect. (1.21.7 G11 stands for 1.21.7 only.)

systemic_note: The 26.1.1 tree is NOT the 1.21.11-template lineage, and it shows: all three 1.21.7 majors (G7 wire class name, G8 push-reaction loader, G9 obsidian hardcode) reproduce in 26.1.1, where the 26.2 tree carries all three fixes. The 26.1.1 tree's level/ code is otherwise byte-near-identical to the verified 26.1 tree (pistons.rs/classes.rs/shapes.rs/place.rs/tests.rs byte-identical; redstone.rs differs only by the diode guard) - the behaviour deltas are concentrated in the table layer: classes.rs has no alias mechanism and no RedStoneWireBlock spelling, and data.rs's push-reaction loader matches only the 26.3 enum names. The 26.2 tree is the natural reference for the G7/G8/G9 repairs. Two 1.21.7 defects (G11, G12) do not apply to 26.1.1 at all - vanilla itself changed between 1.21.7 and 26.1 (comparator takes max(frame, block); moveBlocks destroys with setBlock(air, 18)), and the port matches 26.1.1's form. NEW vs 26.1: the 26.1.1 tree did not inherit the 26.1 tree's level/ behaviour fixes - it carries 26.2/26.3-form behaviour the 26.1 tree deliberately removed. The in-scope instance is B2-G07 (the diode same-block guard); out-of-scope instances (bed use, composter, ice melt, tripwire re-check, sculk tag, motion tags, ensure_block_entity, eyeblossom scan order) are flagged in the report section 6 for their owning batches. PORT-NOTES-26.1.1.md states the carry-forward took the completed 26.1 code as base; the observed level/ state contradicts that for the behaviour fixes. Every batch should diff its scope against the 26.1 tree the way this batch did. The oracle picture matches 26.1's exactly (BlockUpdate broken with 32 errors, Catalog with 4, FaceSupport with 1 blocking the piston-shape cascade), and the three 1.21.7 persistence/piston oracles stay fixed for 26.1.1.
